https://www.dw.com/en/us-man-killed-in-s.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OBlh People were seein being evacuated from the Goliath roller coaster Image: Emilie Megnien/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement One person has died and several others were injured in an incident on Monday involving a roller coaster at a Six Flags theme park in the United States . The incident occurred at Six Flags Over Georgia, about 15 miles (24 kilometers) northwest of Atlanta. Witnesses told local media outlets that they saw a man fall from the ride. "I cannot imagine the horror the patrons and employees witnessed today, and my heart aches for the family who lost a loved one," said Lisa Cupid, chair of the Cobb County Board of Commissioners. Six Flags temporary closes 9 roller coasters Following the incident in Georgia, Six Flags temporarily closed nine roller coasters across six amusement parks. According to a park spokesperson, similar attractions were closed across their parks "out of an abundance of caution" following the incident at Six Flags Over Georgia. This comes less than two weeks after Six Flags Magic Mountain in Southern California announced it would retire its famous X2 roller coaster amid lawsuits alleging the ride caused serious brain injuries. What do we know about the roller coaster? Althought the park did not identify the ride involved in Monday's incident, local media showed passengers being evacuated from the Goliath coaster. Built in 2006, Goliath can reach speeds of 113 km/h (70 mph) and a maximum height of 61 meters (200 feet). According to the theme park's website, riders "navigate through razor-sharp turns and soar over colossal hills." Monday's death would be at least the seventh to occur at the Georgia theme park, according to the Doan Law Firm, which focuses on amusement park accidents. That includes one 2006 incident when a man had a likely heart attack while riding the same roller coaster, Goliath. Edited by: Dmytro Hubenko Don't let the algorithm hide the news. Pakistan: Classrooms reduced to rubble in deadly school disaster, at leat 32 pupils killed Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 15/10/2026 - 15:03 GMT+2 A school roof collapsed in Peshawar, northwestern Pakistan, on Thursday 15 October, killing at least 32 pupils and a teacher. Officials said the roof was structurally weak and had been overloaded by construction work. The school’s owner was arrested and an investigation launched. … More Rescue teams rushed to the scene, where classrooms were left strewn with rubble , school bags, books and children's shoes . Injured pupils were taken by ambulance to Lady Reading Hospital , where medical staff treated survivors as distressed relatives gathered outside. Images from the school show abandoned belongings scattered across the floors, offering a stark glimpse of the devastation left behind by the collapse . ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Peshawar’s police chief said the roof had been weakened by thebuilding’s poor structural condition and the weight of construction work. Heavy rain may also have played a role , but the exact cause remains under investigation. Questions have emerged over whether the tragedy could have been prevented . A father who lost two children told AFP that pupils had reportedly warned the school administration earlier that morning that the building was showing signs of collapse . His account raises concerns about whether warning signs were overlooked before the roof gave way . At the hospital in Peshawar , ambulances continued to bring in casualties as families waited for news of their loved ones. The circumstances surrounding the collapse and the reported warnings have yet to be independently established .
